title: A protein sequence containing a `*` stop codon fails to parse
body:
A user reported that a protein fasta containing `*`, the IUPAC symbol for a stop codon, stops nail during seeding with this error:

```text
indexing query database... done (0.01s)
indexing target database... done (0.01s)
seeding...

error: progessive seeding failed

Caused by:
0: failed to write mmseqs target DB
1: failed to parse record
2: byte: "42" is not in the compressed amino acid alphabet
```

`Sequence::from_fasta` in `libnail/src/structs/sequence.rs` maps each residue byte through `UTF8_TO_DIGITAL_AMINO_TABLE`. It bails on any byte that maps to `UNKNOWN_UTF8_BYTE`, and `*` is one of those. The message gives the byte as a decimal number and names neither the record nor the file. The record fails only when nail writes the mmseqs target DB, after indexing has already reported success.

## Proposal

Read how HMMER and Easel handle `*` in a protein sequence, and match that behaviour as closely as nail can. The minimum is that a `*` at the end of a record parses without an error. An internal `*` may deserve a warning that names the record, for example "internal stop codon detected".

## Open

- how HMMER digitizes `*`, whether it treats a terminal `*` differently from an internal one, and what it scores at that position
- whether mmseqs accepts `*` in the sequence DB nail writes, or nail has to strip or replace it first
- whether the error for any other byte outside the alphabet should name the record and print the character; nail-d551f7 surveys errors like this one

notes.author: Jack Roddy/87ab289b
notes.text:
How HMMER 3.4 and Easel handle `*` in a protein sequence. The source is `hmmer-3.4`. Lines marked checked were read directly, and the rest come from a sub-agent's read.

## Reading

- `esl_sqio_ascii.c:2978` (checked): the fasta reader accepts `*` in every sequence, with the comment "accept * as a nonresidue/stop codon character"
- `*` is digitized to code 27 (Kp-2), the nonresidue code. Nothing strips a terminal `*`, nothing treats it apart from an internal one, and nothing prints a warning.
- a byte outside the alphabet fails with "Line N: illegal character C"

## Scoring a target

- `modelconfig.c:138` (checked): the match score of `*` is -inf
- `modelconfig.c:168` (checked): the generic profile gives an insert -inf for `*`. The SSE filters and the SSE Forward and Backward add no insert emission term at all, so in a default `hmmsearch` run a `*` can sit in an insert state at score 0.
- `generic_fwdback.c:120` (checked): the N, C and J loops never read the residue, so a `*` in a flank costs only the loop transition
- null2 and the bias filter give `*` an odds ratio of 1.0
- from a run of `hmmsearch` by the sub-agent: a terminal `*` on HBB_HUMAN left the score at 216.5 bits and only added 1 to L. An internal `*` dropped the score to 209.6 bits and sat in an insert column inside one domain.

## nail today

nail's digital alphabet already matches Easel's, with `*` at code 27 (`Profile::NON_RESIDUE_IDX`). Only `Sequence::from_fasta` and the maps in `alphabet.rs` lack it. nail leaves the match score of code 27 at -inf and gives every insert column 0, which is what the SSE path does. null2 gives code 27 a ratio of 1.0. mmseqs ran without trouble on targets with a terminal and an internal `*`.

## Queries

`phmmer` accepts `*` in a query as well. A terminal `*` left the top score at 1017.1 bits, and an internal `*` dropped it to 1010.8 bits. `p7_Seqmodel` takes the match emissions at each query position from row `dsq[k]` of its matrix `Q`. Nobody has checked what that row holds for code 27.
